novel_features.name: Voice auditioning
novel_features.description: Generate one sample sentence across every TTS speaker and hear them all side by side
novel_features.rationale: Requires pacing N TTS calls across the speaker catalog with labeled file output — no single API call or existing tool provides auditioning
novel_features.example: sarvam-pp-cli voices preview --lang hi-IN --sample "नमस्ते, स्वागत है" --speakers shubh,ritu,priya --output ./voices
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when choosing a TTS voice for a new language or prompt set without burning manual API calls

novel_features.name: Conversation resume
novel_features.description: Continue a past chat thread from local history with full context
novel_features.rationale: The chat API requires the full message array, which only a local store can replay
novel_features.example: sarvam-pp-cli chat resume 20260814_2d09e061 "what was our conclusion?"
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to continue an assistant session without losing context, offline from the original thread

novel_features.name: Batch job retry
novel_features.description: Re-run only the failed files of a batch STT job with one command
novel_features.rationale: Filters per-file failure state from job details and orchestrates the initiate/upload/start lifecycle — no existing tool does this
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when a batch job partially fails and you need to reprocess just the failures

novel_features.name: Pronunciation spot-check
novel_features.description: Verify a term's TTS pronunciation via a speech round-trip (TTS then STT)
novel_features.rationale: Chains TTS with dict_id and STT to mechanically verify pronunciation dictionaries actually change how a term sounds
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to confirm a pronunciation dictionary edit took effect before shipping IVR prompts

novel_features.name: Subtitle export
novel_features.description: Emit .srt/.vtt subtitles from timestamped transcriptions in local history
novel_features.rationale: Formats timestamped STT output into subtitle cue blocks — a pure local computation no API provides
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to turn a timestamped transcription into subtitles without a throwaway script

novel_features.name: Extraction schema library
novel_features.description: Save, list, and diff doc-ai extraction schemas locally
novel_features.rationale: Stores extraction JSON schemas with versioning in the local store — schemas otherwise live in gists with no diff
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to version extraction schemas so schema changes never silently break extraction runs

novel_features.name: Folder extraction run
novel_features.description: Run a saved extraction schema over a folder of documents with job pacing
novel_features.rationale: Orchestrates the full upload/extract/poll/results lifecycle per file with a saved schema — no competitor CLI offers this
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for weekly batch document extraction (KYC, invoices) without writing orchestration code

novel_features.name: Batch job report
novel_features.description: Per-file digest of a batch STT job with typed exit codes for cron alerting
novel_features.rationale: Transforms job status counts and per-file state into a persisted report with non-zero exit on failure — the dashboard cannot be scripted
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use in cron to alert when a batch transcription job degrades

narrative.headline: Every Sarvam AI model on your terminal — translate, speak, transcribe, chat, and extract documents in 22 Indian languages, with a local history that compounds
narrative.value_prop: Sarvam AI's official SDKs and MCP server are great for code, but nothing offers offline capability: no local history of translations, TTS generations, transcriptions, or chat threads. sarvam-pp-cli adds a local SQLite store, voice auditioning, conversation resume, batch job retry/report, pronunciation spot-checks, subtitle export, and a doc-ai extraction schema library — all with --json, --dry-run, and typed exit codes for agents and scripts.
narrative.auth_narrative: Authentication uses the Sarvam AI API subscription key (sk_ format). Set it with `export SARVAM_API_KEY=sk_...` or `sarvam-pp-cli auth set-token`. The key goes in the `api-subscription-key` header (or `Authorization: Bearer`). Note: an invalid key returns HTTP 403 with `invalid_api_key_error`, not 401 — treat 403 as the auth-failure signal. The separate Voice Agents platform (apps.sarvam.ai) uses a different X-API-Key system and is out of scope for this CLI.

quickstart.comment: Verify the CLI is installed and configured

quickstart.command: sarvam-pp-cli translate --input "Hello, how are you?" --source-language-code en-IN --target-language-code hi-IN
sarvam-pp-cli text-to-speech text-to-speech "नमस्ते, स्वागत है" --language-code hi-IN --speaker shubh
sarvam-pp-cli chat "What is Sarvam AI?" --model sarvam-105b

troubleshoots.fix: The key is invalid or expired — not a 401. Re-run `sarvam-pp-cli auth set-token` with a fresh key from the Sarvam dashboard.
pitch and loudness are bulbul:v2-only. Use `--model bulbul:v2` or drop those flags.

troubleshoots.symptom: Chat returns content: null with only reasoning
troubleshoots.fix: Set `--max-tokens` explicitly — hidden reasoning can consume the token budget before content.
mayura:v1 caps at 1000 chars. Use `--model sarvam-translate:v1` for up to 2000 chars.
Sarvam uses token-bucket limits (translate 60/min, TTS 60/min, chat 40/min on sarvam-105b). Add pacing or retry with backoff.

narrative.when_to_use: Use sarvam-pp-cli when you need to translate, transliterate, transcribe, synthesize speech, chat, or extract document fields through Sarvam AI's Indic-language models — especially when you want a record of what you did, offline search across past work, batch orchestration, or scriptable/agent-friendly output. It is the right tool for voice-agent prompt engineering, call-center transcription QA, content localization, and document-intelligence pipelines.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI for the Voice Agents platform (apps.sarvam.ai) — deployments, campaigns, cohorts, analytics, and instant outbound use a separate X-API-Key auth system with org/workspace scoping and are not implemented here.
Do not use this CLI for real-time WebSocket streaming (realtime STT, TTS WS) — those are AsyncAPI surfaces not covered by the REST CLI.
Do not use this CLI to replace a full speech-recognition model benchmark — the API is a paid service and the CLI does not add model-evaluation tooling.
